floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 8 confirmed; 8 diffs are TWO independent reg-alloc/scheduling ties (inner sum/j $a0 swap; 2nd-loop LICM-const vs move preheader order) — both pure-C, greg-characterized, frontier built.
Region A quantified as a pure sum/j $a0<->$a1 swap (all surroundings match target); naive structural levers KILLED, pointing to the directed permuter.

Region A range-mechanism CONFIRMED: offset+=j flips the sum/j a0/a1 swap (score 7) but is not match-viable; zero-cost manual flips killed, so the flip needs the directed permuter's whole-function LUID
Directed permuter (real full-TU basin) found do-while(0) on sum=0 that solves Region A and lowers the honest floor 8->6; Region B has no clean permuter lever (all sub-130 finds invalid).
Fresh-seed floor-6 permuter (20.9k iters) + exhaustive preheader lineswap reconfirm no clean lever: Region A' tie unreachable by statement reorder, Region B yields only dead-alias cheats.

frontier.hypothesis: The Region A' preheader tie can be flipped by a whole-function context change that raises bp's addu priority above the sum/j moves in the preheader BB, without a preheader statement reorder (all reorders killed) and without disturbing the solved Region A allocation.
frontier.mechanism: The tie lives in cc1 sched1 (basic-block list scheduler) over the outer-loop-body preheader BB; the emit order is set by INSN_PRIORITY / absolute LUID, which is a whole-function effect (manual reorder only rotates the three inits' relative LUID, insufficient).
frontier.next_probe: Instrument cc1 with BB2_SCHED_DEBUG (tmp/gccdbg/cc1) on the floor-6 build and read the priorities/LUIDs of bp's addu vs the two moves in the preheader BB; identify what upstream context lifts bp's addu (e.g. a legitimately-earlier real consumer of bp) that isn't a dead store.

frontier.hypothesis: Region B closes only via a loop-shape change that legitimately computes the pointer-range bound before the ap/a2p moves, materializing the two LICM constants at lower LUID than the moves without a constant-holder or dead-alias cheat.
frontier.mechanism: LICM hoists the two constants to preheader END (higher LUID) so sched1 ties to the lower-LUID ap/a2p moves; the target had them at lower LUID. No source form referencing the constants only inside the loop can move them earlier without a cheat.
frontier.next_probe: Design and sandbox a Region B loop shape where the range test's invariant is part of a genuinely loop-carried/hoisted computation with a real dependency chain to the pointer moves (raising the moves' LUID above the constants), vetting every candidate against the constant-holder / dead-alias cheat catalog before proposing.
